messages:
Priya Rao: heads-up: Sequoia (prod) opened a ticket — p99 jumped from ~420ms to ~1.8s after the runtime deploy at 2026-03-16T03:12Z. Affects multiple routes.

Priya Rao: @Alex Chen can you triage? They're on dedicated pool ded-47.

ops-bot: [alert] customer/sequoia: latency_p99 threshold breached (1.8s) — triggered 2026-03-16T03:45:12Z :warning:

Alex Chen: taking this. Quick plan: 1) repro with internal bench on ded-47 image 2) compare p99 pre/post commits 3) lightweight profile (nsys/perf) 4) check KV cache hit/miss.

David Morales: I can run a private bench using a copied workload. Which model + seq?

Priya Rao: Sequoia runs rlm-small-7b, typical seq 512 (occasionally 1024). Start with 512 and concurrency 4/8/16. Also check continuous batching — last deploy changed batch.max_delay -> 12ms.

Alex Chen: running reproduce tool on a staging ded-47 vm:
```
./bench/run_workload --model rlm-small-7b --seq 512 --concurrency 8 --tokens 50000 --pool ded-47 --trace perf
```

Alex Chen: initial (old-image) run p99 ~450ms. Current image run shows p99 ~1.7s reproducible. Uploading nsys dump to #eng-runtime/artifacts.

Sara López: infra metrics: KV cache hit ratio on ded-47 dropped 0.95 -> 0.62 roughly at deploy time. Also saw CPU steal spike on host h-301 around the same window.

David Morales: I ran bench with --no_kv_cache and saw p99 ~1.6s as well. Points to caching or batching logic, not just cache misses.

Alex Chen: profiler quick summary: softmax kernel consuming ~68% of time, attention-roll ~12%, memcpy ~8%. Looks like the kernel-selector picked a different softmax path (float32) on the new selection.

Priya Rao: @Marco (oncall) any kernel-selector rollouts around 03:00Z? Could ks changes explain this?

Marco (oncall): yes, we rolled kernel-selector v2 at 03:05Z; feature flag ks-v2 -> 100% on dedicated pools. Rolling it back for ded-47 now.

ops-bot: [deploy-bot] rolled featureflag ks-v2=0 for pool=ded-47 (initiated by Marco) — 2026-03-16T04:02:01Z

Alex Chen: re-ran bench post-rollback — p99 back to ~430ms. Confirmed ks-v2 selection caused the regression; new softmax kernel slower on this GPU/driver combo for small batches.

Sara López: note in radar: driver 525.60 + CUDA 12.2 + ks-v2 => softmax regression for small batch sizes. We'll add a driver-based avoid-list for ks-v2.

Priya Rao: action items: 
- Alex: PR to gate ks-v2 by driver/kernel + add kernel blacklist (owner: Alex) — due EOD.
- David: run a quick matrix (seq 256/512/1024 x conc 4/8/16) and upload CSV (owner: David) — due in 2h.
- Marco: add canary for ks-v2 on dedicated pools via deploy service (owner: Marco) — start today.
- Support: notify Sequoia about the rollback and follow-up plan (owner: support-bot). :thumbsup:

support-bot: Notified #customer-success/sequoia and created a follow-up ticket referencing rollback + next steps.

Alex Chen: PR opened https://git.internal.redwood/infra/ks-selector/pulls/218 — adds driver checks + unit test. Requesting review from @Sara López and @David Morales.

David Morales: uploaded matrix results to artifacts/sqc-2026-03-16/bench.csv — added notes on --no_kv_cache runs.

Priya Rao: keeping thread open for follow-ups. If anyone finds an alternate mitigation (patching kernel, selective fallback) post here.

Alex Chen: will attach flamegraphs to PR and close the loop with CS after merge.
